verdict.reasoning: Doctor summarizes: “last three days, you've been having bit of burning pain on passing urine,” and patient earlier describes it as “sort of like a stinging kind of pain… when I pee.”
Patient: “there was a little bit of blood earlier today” and “It does kind of… doesn't smell very, it smells a bit weird I guess,” which supports a small episode of hematuria and malodorous urine.

Patient: “maybe sometimes get some like, pain kind of lower down in my tummy, when I, when I go to the bathroom” (mild lower abdominal pain with voiding) and denies pain moving to back or flank: “No, not really, no.”

Patient denies increased frequency: “Um, not, I don't think so, I haven't noticed that.” Nocturia/urgency not explicitly asked but not reported. Denies nausea/vomiting: “Uh, no, not, not at all.” Denies fever: “No, no, no fever, no.” Reports normal bowels and no diarrhea: “I think so… it seems…,” “no, not that I've noticed at all.” Absence of urgency/nocturia is consistent with not being discussed or reported.
Patient: “yeah I am” (sexually active) and “I've had a boyfriend for about a, a couple of months now,” and on contraception: “Uh, yeah, we use condoms.”

No discharge: Patient: “I haven't noticed anything” when asked about discharge. LMP: “Uh, couple of weeks ago.” Doctor restates: “Three weeks ago, OK.” Pregnancy: Patient says, “Uh, I don't think so, I don't,” when asked about chance of pregnancy.
Patient: “in the past I've had some uh, some IBS.”
Patient: “Do you take any regular medications?… Uh, no,” and “I did… try some uh, over the counter bicarbonate… but it wasn't really helping.”
Patient: “I'm allergic to, Clindamycin.” and “I get some like a, a, a swelling, basically.”

Living situation: “I live in a flat near my college, with a, a couple of like friends of mine.” Student/major: “I'm a student… I'm studying biology.” Smoking/alcohol: “I don't, I don't smoke, uh, I do drink, like on the weekends, yeah.”

Doctor assessment: “I think probably do have what we call a simple UTI or urinary tract infection, bladder infection,” in the context of dysuria and small hematuria episodes, which corresponds to uncomplicated cystitis.
As above, allergy documented: “I'm allergic to, Clindamycin… I get… swelling,” supporting the statement that she has a clindamycin allergy.
Transcript only states past IBS: “in the past I've had some… IBS,” with no comment on current symptom status or stability, so calling it “stable” adds new information.
Doctor: “I'll give you a course of antibiotics today. Something, called either Nitrofurantoin, or Trimethoprim… it's normally a three day course. Uh, so, one tablet, twice a day, for three days.”
Doctor: “I also advise you to drink plenty of fluids… You can try, cranberry juice, that can sometimes help with your symptoms.”
Doctor: “if you can try and avoid [sex], I think that'd be sensible… I would recommend you to continue using barrier contraception, but if you can avoid it while your symptoms clear up.”

Doctor: “if you're still not better, by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me,” and later: “things to look out for would be… high temperatures, a back pain… generally feeling more unwell… do give me a call if you're having any concerns.”
Doctor: “if… you are worried about the pain… I'd always advise getting a pregnancy test, to rule out pregnancy,” which corresponds to performing a urine pregnancy test if there is concern.
